author: WP11
summary: Compares the three non-WebGL browser renderers by object model: Canvas 2D pixels, pooled CSS elements and retained SVG, with their capability answers, 3D refusal policies and evidence tiers. Mostly current, but it describes the DOM renderers' targets as DOM-backed (they are canvas-backed), omits the opt-in host contract suites and counts thirteen capabilities. Tutorial 105 already covered choice and performance; a new deep dive adds the source-level object models, refusals and evidence matrix.

sections.heading: Built tests are not registered tests
HTML_DOM: sprites as pooled CSS objects
The strongest browser evidence in this cluster

concepts.text: CANVAS, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM render XNA-style sprites in a browser without WebGL: Canvas 2D pixels, pooled CSS-transformed elements, and retained SVG image nodes with filters; all are Emscripten-only and 2D-only, with different object models and evidence.

target.evidence: cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (Emscripten gate); the three families' sources

concepts.text: CANVAS reports additive blending true ('lighter'); HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM answer with the browser's CSS.supports('mix-blend-mode', 'plus-lighter'); all three support RenderTarget2D but not MRT or queries.

CANVAS obtains getContext('2d') and maps texture uploads and sprites onto drawImage, putImageData and fillRect; a texture is a private OffscreenCanvas and a RenderTarget2D is another Canvas 2D surface.
CANVAS has no shader stage, depth buffer, MRT, query or 3D path; its 3D hooks use HandleUnsupported3DCall, so WarnAndStub is honoured and resource factories return stubs under it.
concepts.note: The source said inherited draws end in the explicit refusal; the WarnAndStub path is the TARGET qualification.

concepts.text: Answering only AdditiveBlending lets callers discover the 2D ceiling before constructing unsupported objects, which is more useful than the renderer contract's permissive default.
concepts.note: The source counted thirteen capability flags; there are 19 at 009d40f5.

concepts.section: Built tests are not registered tests
concepts.text: Canvas test executables are built but deliberately not registered with CTest, so a green host run says nothing about Canvas pixels; an opt-in native host contract suite (CanvasHostContracts) exists behind CNA_BUILD_CANVAS_HOST_TESTS.
concepts.note: The host contract suite is a TARGET addition the source did not mention.

concepts.section: Built tests are not registered tests
concepts.text: Node alone cannot run the Canvas programs (SDL video init fails with no browser DOM); a meaningful run opens the page in a real or headless browser, drives frames and reads pixels or a screenshot.

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: sprites as pooled CSS objects
concepts.text: HTML_DOM keeps a pool of elements: sprite n of a batch lands on pool element n, each element caches its last CSS values, and moving sprites write only transform and opacity, so reuse avoids unbounded allocation and forced layout.

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: sprites as pooled CSS objects
concepts.text: Browser compositing is part of HTML_DOM's contract: each scissor rectangle gets its own region and pool, painter's order across regions uses a per-flush z-index, and additive blending depends on plus-lighter support.
concepts.note: The source equated ordering with DOM stacking order; at 009d40f5 cross-region order is an explicit z-index.

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: sprites as pooled CSS objects
concepts.text: HTML_DOM's off-screen target is a Canvas 2D context into which the same command array is replayed, not a DOM subtree; back-buffer readback throws while target readback is a real getImageData.
concepts.note: The source called the target DOM-backed; it is canvas-backed at 009d40f5.

concepts.section: HTML_DOM: sprites as pooled CSS objects
concepts.text: HTML_DOM's 3D and unsupported-state refusals go through a local [[noreturn]] ThrowNo3D and bypass the shared WarnAndStub policy, so they always throw.

concepts.section: The strongest browser evidence in this cluster
concepts.text: HTML_DOM has the strongest browser evidence: htmldom-ci.yml drives smoke, pixel, stress, dispose, host-integration and memory pages in headless Chromium through Playwright under Xvfb on every push; its native host contract target is opt-in and not run by CI, and DOM node counts prove a different layer from composited pixels.
concepts.note: The source presented the host contract target alongside CI; it is off by default at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: SVG_DOM builds a retained tree of pooled <g> sprites with nested <svg>/<image> crops or pattern-filled rects, tints with a cached feColorMatrix filter and marks additive sprites with mix-blend-mode plus-lighter behind the same CSS.supports answer.

SVG_DOM's retained tree is inspectable and suits vector composition but inherits SVG's filter, sampling, blending and layout semantics; only Linear and Point filters are accepted and Clamp overflow or mixed addressing throws.
tokens: inherits SVG's filter, sampling, blending and layout semantics

concepts.text: Like HTML_DOM, SVG_DOM has an off-screen Canvas 2D target, no MRT or queries, a refused back-buffer readback and a 3D refusal that bypasses WarnAndStub.
concepts.note: The source called the target DOM-backed; it is canvas-backed at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: SVG_DOM's browser pages (smoke with CSS support, capability and sprite style; pixel; scissor order) run only through the manual run-svgdom-browser-test.sh, and its host contract target sits behind the off-by-default CNA_BUILD_SVG_DOM_HOST_TESTS with no workflow.

The three fail in different places: Canvas around pixel upload, context state, clipping and composite operations; HTML_DOM around pooling, CSS transforms, stacking and plus-lighter; SVG_DOM around retained-node lifetime, transforms, filters and sampling.

A cross-renderer browser scene should include crop, origin-centred rotation, alpha and additive overlap, clipping, target bind/unbind and node-count stability over frames, inspecting both structure and pixels.

A browser renderer report records the identity, Emscripten version, browser and version, device-pixel ratio, canvas or SVG size and visible or headless execution, confirms several animation frames and treats compilation only as the first gate.

issues.text: CANVAS has no automated browser execution: its programs are built but unregistered and its host contract suite is opt-in and not run by any workflow.
SVG_DOM browser pages run only through a manual script, and its host contract suite is opt-in with no workflow.
HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM additive blending silently degrades to ordinary composition on browsers without mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter.
HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM cannot read back the back buffer; a readback region larger than a smaller bound target returns transparent padding (accepted gap).
